Jabra Evolve 65e Wireless Neckband Headset, Link 370, MS-Optimized – Bluetooth Headset with up to 13 Hours of Battery Life – Superior Sound for Calls and Music – Passive Noise Cancelling Headset I ordered the 'Jabra Evolve 65e UC & Link 370 Wireless Professional Earbuds' as I'm a sucker for trying out new wireless earbuds. I've tried various different types. Some that are "truly wireless", some like these that have the connected wire around the neck. These Jabra Evolve 65e earbuds are really pretty amazing for what they are. Sound is great but not booming with bass. They are crisp yet not loud. There is really no sound isolation as the buds don't fit snug in the ear, (even trying the included different size tips and wings) but that seems to be on purpose. As from I can tell from reading about these, is that they are meant to allow some outside sound, so that if you are say jogging, you should be able to hear to be safe right? Now with that said, I see the purpose and the market for these earbuds, and there is absolute value to these.
Pairing these to my Android mobile phone was an absolute breeze. Also, using the USB Bluetooth adapter on my Chromebook made pairing these super simple as well.
Call quality is on par with most wireless earbuds. It's good, but not the same as just using your phone obviously but better than some "cheap" buds I've tried. These are definitely built with the Jabra quality you would expect and I'm overall impressed.
They fit comfortably and secure and I've had no issue with them popping out, but then again I'm not a jogger. They are easy to fit into your ears, unlike others that I've had that take a bit of twisting to get the fit just right.
The app is nice and works well but as with most apps like this, it's gimmicky. I mean I've played with it a bit at first but any more, I just pop the buds in and go, and haven't used the app in quite a while.
So to summarize, these are great earbuds if you don't need "truly wireless" and you don't need sound isolation.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65e Wireless Neckband Headset, Link 370, MS-Optimized – Bluetooth Headset with up to 13 Hours of Battery Life – Superior Sound for Calls and Music – Passive Noise Cancelling Headset

SIN SHINE - Compressed Air 3.0- Multi-Use Electric Air Duster for Cleaning Dust, Hairs, Crumbs, Scraps for Laptop, Computer, Replaces Compressed Air Cans (AD01-Black) I use canned dusters for a variety of purposes, from cleaning keyboards to cleaning up my electric shaver. These sometimes leave residue behind, so I was interested in trying this electric duster to see if it would cut down on residue and save money in the long run. I will confess that I was not very optimistic and thought it would be underpowered. However, it has proven to be as effective as a canned duster in cleaning keyboards and other equipment, without leaving any residue and without losing power like canned dusters tend to do as they get cold.

This device is smaller than a tea kettle and relatively light. It requires an AC outlet so it does need to be plugged in when you want to use it. I was hopeful I had missed something on the description and that there was a rechargeable battery but unfortunately this is not the case. This was me being hopeful, not a confusing write-up.

It comes with a few attachments to help direct the air flow over the surface of what you’re trying to clean. The most helpful attachment, to me, is the round nozzle, but all of them have their uses.

I took it to my office where we have an abundance of dirty keyboards that need to be cleaned, and I set to work. I was expecting it to do a mediocre cleaning job, but it gave me a very pleasant surprise and blew air with plenty of force to clean out the clumps of dust that collect under the keys. More importantly, though, the power didn’t diminish like what tends to happen with canned dusters as they get cold, and there was no problem with frost buildup either.

So far, this is proving to be a useful and helpful tool. It produces enough force to get the job done without losing power, and it leaves no residue behind.
text_fidelity_b: SIN SHINE - Compressed Air 3.0- Multi-Use Electric Air Duster for Cleaning Dust, Hairs, Crumbs, Scraps for Laptop, Computer, Replaces Compressed Air Cans (AD01-Black)

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens First of all, I would like to start with highly recommending this camera to ANYONE who wants premium image quality with expandability, power and flexibility.

Pentax is one of the only companies out there that is driven entirely by photography and NOT by a marketing department that makes outrageous claims. To this end, even this, their lowest-end camera, is PACKED with premium features. Let's take a look at them:

1. Dust Reduction: Dust WILL get into your camera! This keeps it off of the sensor and increases the time inbetween cleanings.

2. Shake Reduction: It's good for a couple of stops of shooting leeway and you get it with every lens you use. Other companies build their systems into the lenses, meaning ONE lens can cost as much or more than the camera, itself! Lens-based anti-shake systems are more effective at long zoom than body-based systems, but unless you're rich, you won't be able to afford a suite of good lenses! With this camera, you can use ANY Pentax lens and get anti-shake.

3. AA batteries: Proprietary battery packs are NO GOOD. Hmmm, if you're on a shoot and your pack dies, you're not taking ANY photos unless you get a spare, right? With this camera, pick up some 2500mAh Ni-MH AA's and you can afford to get three sets. However, the power drain is so small, you might not need more than one set.

4. 6 MP sensor: Don't EVER get trapped in the megapixel hype. Megapixels mean nothing in the DSLR game, except for noise issues. Let me explain. The sensor sizes on almost all DSLRs (except for $5000 full-frame pro cameras) are APS-sized, meaning the sensor size on this camera and the Nikon D300 are very nearly the same dimensions. This means that photosensors on the chip have to be made smaller to get more pixels...meaning that the closer together/smaller sites are LESS light sensitive and they will also interfere with each other. 6 MP is a perfect sweet spot for noise and image sharpness. You get a base ISO of 200, meaning your camera is TWICE as sensitive to light as one with a base ISO of 100! This camera records color accurately and makes prints up to 8.5"x11" with no problem.

This camera has huge features and, even with the release of the K20D and K200D cameras, still maintains a good feature/image quality set with a proven CCD sensor and a suite of easy-to-learn features and settings. I LOVE this camera and even though I have a K200D for the weather sealing and larger burst capacity, the K100D super is the camera I ALWAYS take with me in trips. You're better off getting this camera plus a really nice lens and a 360FZ flash than a more expensive camera with a base kit lens and no external flash.

Believe me, this camera's quality will not fail to impress you and it will grow with you. It can use ANY lens its bigger brothers can and it uses them effortlessly.

A superb camera and one for the record books!
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics microSDXC Memory Card with Full Size Adapter, A2, U3, Read Speed up to 100 MB/s, 64 GB, Pack of 2, Black I selected this memory card because I needed one for a dash cam. When it comes to storage, name bands are usually the way to go when you need something really reliable, so I was a little hesitant at first to use a "store brand" card. So far, it has been fine and I have no complaints, though it will take time and more use to determine if it will hold up long-term.

The card I received is a 128GB MicroSD with an adapter. The adapter makes it work in a camera like my mirrorless, but I would not recommend this kind of set-up unless pressed. The adapter is really most useful when pulling data from the card in a machine that does not have a slot for a MicroSD, so the adapter does have its place.

The card fit in my dash cam with no issues and the cam seems to be happy with it. It detects the presence of the card and the full capacity of it which is good. Being a class 10 card it is fast enough to keep up with the recording and in a 45 minute trip it did not skip or stutter once. Quality seems to be fine. Using the adapter, my PC has no trouble reading the card and reformatting when I want to quickly erase it.

So far, this card has worked out just fine and I am pleased with it. It's priced well and it seems to work well in the way I need it to work. Time will tell if it will hold up, but so far all indicators are positive.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics microSDXC Memory Card with Full Size Adapter, A2, U3, Read Speed up to 100 MB/s, 64 GB, Pack of 2, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Medialink Wireless Router - Renewed (150 Mbps) - Easy YouTube Setup Video (Part# MWNWAPR150N) I purchased this router to create a small two-computer network in my apartment. My PC is a refurbished and souped up Gateway running Windows Vista, and I bought an older Toshiba laptop, also refurbished and running Windows XP Home Edition. I wanted to be able to sit in my living room or on the patio while working once in awhile, rather than being chained to my home office PC. No gaming consoles, DVRs, or other components to connect.

The setup literature and accompanying CD shipped with the router are invaluable, easy to understand, even for a non-techie like me. However, don't expect your setup to proceed with no glitches! You may have to reset your cable modem two or three times, or restart the various components two or three times. Take your time, follow directions, keep your wits about you, and think about possible causes and likely solutions and you should have no trouble setting up this router.

The day after my order, I also received a lengthy, substantive email from Mediabridge Products, thanking me for my order and supplying me with all kinds of background, links, and telephone technical support information, so I felt confident that I had resources handy during the setup if necessary. So far the router is working like a charm. I recommend it, especially if you're interested in a fairly simple LAN setup!

D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card

text_fidelity_a:
3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD Prior to getting this NVR system, I had already started researching on POE switches. For some reason, I assumed all NVR cameras are POE. I knew this Dragon Touch NVR had no POE ports in the back, but it didn't matter because I had planned to use POE switches. If you're a newbie like me, here are some noteworthy things before you make your decision:

1. The four cameras in this set comes with four power adapters. I thought how nice of them to include this option. But as it turns out, this is NOT an option. You need to use the power adapters for each camera. I learned that getting POE switches is only half the battle, the other half is making sure the cameras are POE compatible. I didn't know that. I thought POE switches would allow me to get rid of power adapters to any camera, any brand. Sadly, this is not the case. So this Dragon Touch system is designed for wi-fi. You only need to hook up the power adapter to each camera. But the whole point of me going to NVR is to use ethernet for more dependable connections. You can still do that with this system, but you'll still need to connect the power adapters, so you're running two cables for each camera. Had I known that, I would not have gotten this system.

2. You can use other brand cameras with this NVR if the cameras are ONVIF. However, I'm betting they still need to be the non-POE kind. I'm trying to connect a H.View POE camera, but I'm getting a black screen. Dragon Touch said that model is not compatible. End of email. I had to follow up with "What POE cameras are compatible?" I'll update when they respond.

3. It goes without saying, but in case you don't know, you need to connect NVR to a monitor for viewing. The back of the NVR has options for VGA or HDMI out. Alternatively, you can view via their Homeviz app.

4. No hard drive is included, but a hard drive is not necessary for you to start learning, testing, and setting things up. You can live view without a hard drive, but to record you'll need to install a hard drive.

5. Lastly, I'll talk about the build quality of this system. The Dragon Touch is very professionally packaged, the NVR is small and light, but that's without a hard drive currently. The cameras feel real nice, has good heft to them. I am not going to subtract any stars because of my newbie assumptions. As a matter of fact, I'm learning that if you want NVR systems with POE cameras, they would be much more expensive than what you're paying here. If I can figure a way to run both ethernet and power adapters, I may end up using this system. However, I will subtract a star for the lack of info in their listing, and emails. A product like this should clearly state whether or not their cameras are POE, and whether or not the NVR can handle POE cameras. 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: 3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all.

I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black

text_fidelity_a:
ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do.

In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.
text_fidelity_b: ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count

Of course I still get plenty of sales calls from somewhat legitimate companies from numbers that obviously aren't stored in the machine already.  When you receive a call, there is a BLOCK NOW button you can press to block the call in the future.  Unfortunately it only works about half the time.  Can't say that I have ever gotten "#2" from any of my phones to work, which is supposed to also block calls, as well as pushing the BLOCK NOW button.  The price is probably not worth it for a device that only partly solves the problem.  There are probably less expensive ways to deal with unwanted calls, although I don't have a good solution, which is why I got this device.  Granted my phone system is set up a little strange, so that could be part of the problem with this working as well as it could.  Also, the device needs a way to be updated to add more scam numbers as they are identified.  Seems to me that in a few years there could be many more numbers that aren't already stored in the unit.  The unit is a great idea, but it needs some work.  Probably works best with just one or two telephones, but I have phones all over the house; some are corded and some are cordless.  I have great hopes for the next model of this device if they make some good improvements.  Can't quite recommend it yet, unless you have an extreme problem with unwanted calls.  It probably will cut down on the unwanted calls, so might be worth it to get it, even if it helps only a little.
text_fidelity_b: CPR V10000 - Landline Phone Call Blocker with Dual Mode Protection. Pre-Loaded with 10,000 Known Robocall Scam Numbers - Block a Further 2,000 Numbers at a Touch of a Button

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.

This was extremely helpful when one of my battery backups suddenly expired--taking down telephone and Internet service--and needed immediate replacement. (There was NO need to open the UPS battery compartment and fiddle with the terminals before plugging the UPS in.)

To my surprise, the Liebert UPS has a liquid crystal display that shows the battery charge before the unit is plugged in (new out of the box, my battery was about 85% charged). After the unit is plugged in, the LCD has "icons and numerical information to display UPS status and operational parameters" (e.g., input, output, total load). There is a built-in input circuit breaker that trips if the output load exceeds the unit's power rating.

The UPS even has a button you can press to turn off the beeping during a power outage! Because my area experiences frequent inexplicable outages (ranging from less than a minute to a few hours) this feature alone is enough to make me buy Lieberts from now on.

The outlets are conveniently placed on the unit. There are four surge protection plus battery backup outlets (outlets that keep your computer and critical electronics operating on battery power for a few minutes into an outage), and four surge protection only outlets. One of each type of outlet is placed slightly apart from the others, to make space for extra-large plugs.

I don't use the software that usually comes with a UPS, but this Liebert UPS includes a CD with documentation and optional software, a 6-1/2 ft. coaxial cable (for TV), and a 3 ft. USB cable (for computer). There are ports for telephone lines as well.

This is a beautifully designed UPS with all the expected features, and with some great unexpected features.
text_fidelity_b: Vertiv Liebert 500VA 300W Battery Backup & Surge Protector, 6-Outlet, 3 Year Warranty, TAA Compliant (PST4-500MT120)

Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100) I intended to give the [[ASIN:B00AQRUW4Q Seagate Wireless Plus 1 TB Mobile Device Storage with Built-In Wi-Fi Streaming (STCK1000100)]] a rating of four stars, but have decided that it really is a five star product. The near deduction was because of the frustration I experienced in my attempting to get the device up and running with the limited information provided in the package and on the website. Once I successfully downloaded the software to my Droid, Kindle Fire and MacBook, I still encountered more trial and error than usual until I was able to figure out how the darn thing works. Fast forward to days and weeks of loving the device!

The Wireless Plus can be used as an extra drive for storage if you're not interested in using it for streaming, but if that's your true need, I'd likely recommend purchasing something else. With it's own Wi-Fi streaming, you don't need to use your home or hot network. Using it's Wi-Fi has been quick and has been glitch free for us thus far. We have used three devices at once and found it to be problem-free, with no freezes, crashes or difficulties. We had it up and running for four hours and still had battery power, then recharged. Although it can be charged via the USB on your computer, it is much faster by plugging it into an electrical outlet if one's available. Since we haven't drained the battery yet, I can't say how long it really lasts.

Music, movies, pictures, documents, audiobook, you can use whichever you want on any networked device as long as the device has the appropriate application installed. I watched the Seagate tutorials several times and found them to be difficult to follow, however once I spent some dedicated time just feeling my way through, I discovered that I do like the applications, too. Even if I'm not accessing the Wireless Plus on my Droid, I have been using the Seagate app.

This arrives with little documentation, but it is USB 3 capable if you need it. The housing is lightly rubberized and it has a matte metal plate in a charcoal gray color on the face side. The plug appears to be proprietary, the second reason I almost deducted a star from this review. It looks like a hybrid mini plug that's attached via a thin wire, not a cable, to a USB for either a device or the two prong electrical plug. No case is included, but I have a couple that work great. The size isn't so big that it feels cumbersome, but it is heavier than it appears to be upon first glance. I don't mind the weight because this little device holds 1 TB, much more than I have loaded on it as of today. I highly recommend this device and look forward to Seagate upgrading it as time passes. It's unique and not expensive for what it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100)

The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.
text_fidelity_b: myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output

Wsky 60-100 Miles Transparent Digital HDTV Antenna - Best HDTV Antenna Indoor - Upgraded Silver Paddle Extremely High Reception - Support 1080P 4K Super Fun and Free for Life! My title for this review is not deliberately obtuse, it is just that I was desperate for an antenna and chose the one with the reviews that seemed to best meet my housing needs (apartment) as well as my budgetary needs (retired with small, fixed income).

You know, these small antenna types can only provide as well as they can, given their limited powers and whatever physical/geographic challenges are caused by one's limits on where the thing can be placed.

I do not live surrounded by mountains or trees or large buildings. I do not live in a valley or in the middle of nowhere. I DO live within forty miles of every transmission source in a nearby big city, so it might be considered reasonable to expect that an antenna that touts a sixty-mile range to be useful.

It is, but only partially because the fault is not in our stars, it is in a huge menu of influences (which may include the some sky/heavenly/ astronomical stuff, but that is another story).

My point, and the useful part, is that these simple and, more importantly, cheap antennas can only do what they can because geography, distance, obstacles you cannot see or image and even the stars (yep) conspire to modify their successful use, and even all that can be affected by other stuff we are unable to anticipate or influence.

If you want an antenna that has a potential for reasonable performance, simply spend the considerable dollars that will buy a reasonably and consistent performance.

Sellers, provide honest claims so that purchasers will know what they are getting. Customers, be discerning so that you can use your dollars to get the best you and your critical thinking can provide.

As for me, hope springs eternal that I will someday be able afford an antenna that allows me to watch our local PBS stations and in the meantime I will ignore the religious (not aligned with my personal spiritual practices) and selling-stuff channels.

It is the best I can afford, and a little late-night cartoons never hurt anyone.

The four-star rating is only because I finally hold a decent perspective on all this jazz.
text_fidelity_b: Wsky 60-100 Miles Transparent Digital HDTV Antenna - Best HDTV Antenna Indoor - Upgraded Silver Paddle Extremely High Reception - Support 1080P 4K Super Fun and Free for Life!
